correctness.rationale: The signed Laplacian is positive semidefinite. Deleting a vertex and applying a convergent diagonally dominant Neumann series proves absolute inverse domination by the unsigned principal resolvent. Its Schur complement gives h_i>=min(0,2G_ii-1). PSD comparison with the complete-graph Laplacian proves G_ii>=2/(n+1), and hostile-hub substitution gives equality. Exact 729-case finite enumeration verifies the structural four-vertex criterion and all orbit multiplicities using rational elimination. No finite check is used as proof for unbounded graph orders.

originality.rationale: The July 2024 signed Friedkin–Johnsen paper already derives the signed resolvent and observes negative structure centrality. Neither its Sections II and V-A nor the inspected October 2024 signed absolute-influence study gives the uniform sharp lower bound (3-n)/(n+1), hostile-hub equality family, or the complete minimal four-vertex graph census. The 2023 signed-FJ stability paper and the 2019 signed-network survey address distinct statements. Targeted literature and published-finding queries did not reveal a logically dominating result; potential general signed-resolvent inequalities remain a specific priority risk. A 2025 signed-FJ wisdom-of-crowds study was also inspected; it uses the repelling signed-degree Laplacian and a variance objective, rather than the opposing signless-degree Laplacian and sharp aggregate-influence extremum considered here.

value.rationale: Negative signed structure centrality is a natural interpretation problem for the published FJ aggregate objective; its worst possible magnitude across all simple n-person networks was not specified in the motivating source. The sharp formula provides a topology-independent bound on aggregate-opinion reversal, is attained by an explicit antagonistic minority hub, and proves the smallest network scale where nonnegative innate positions can produce a negative public aggregate. The exhaustive first layer identifies all minimal graph structures capable of doing so rather than an arbitrary slice.
